defects.what: The duplicate question is not tuned. I isolated the fifth call and ran all 18 seed pairs: the shipped DUPLICATE_STATEMENT + DUPLICATE_HINTS score 11/18 raw, and every one of the 7 misses is a false positive - it answers 'same event' for distinct emergencies 145 m to 344 m apart (R20 cyclist 0.69, R24 seizure 0.72, R25 water main 0.74, R29 admin call 0.73, R30 car fire 0.62, R31 fall 0.75, R32 power line 0.69). The same-kind guard in buildDecision hides 3 of them, but same-category pairs sail through: the smoke run visibly merges R24 ('kid had a seizure at 31 Quay St') into INC-006 and R31 ('elderly woman fell down the stairs') into INC-011. In a dispatch console a false merge means a real patient's incident is swallowed and no ambulance rolls for it - the exact failure the demo's headline feature is supposed to prevent. I also confirmed the judgment is proximity, not identity: a heart-attack call 90 m from an open apartment fire scores 0.67.
defects.fix: Tighten the pair statement and hints in triage.ts. Verified on the same 18 pairs: DUPLICATE_STATEMENT = "The new report is another call about the very same incident that is already open.", DUPLICATE_HINTS = { when_true: "The same people and the same emergency, reported again or updated.", when_false: "A separate emergency, even at the same address or on the same block." } scores 16/18 raw (every true follow-up still lands 0.62-0.90, and R20/R25/R30/R31/R32 drop to 0.40-0.58). With the existing same-kind guard on top that is ~17/18 end to end. Update the matching hint text in the /yes-no duplicate bullet of src/pages/dispatch.astro.

defects.what: buildDecision vetoes the model's non_emergency label unconditionally: `if (category === "non_emergency" && heuristic.category !== "non_emergency") category = heuristic.category;`. The label is shipped in CATEGORY_LABELS but can never be the output unless the narrow NONEMERGENCY regex agrees, so one of the seven answers the demo advertises is dead. The veto fires above the confidence gate, so lowConfidence stays false and neither the feed chip nor the hover card's '-> keywords' note marks the override. On the seed data this is visible twice: R23 (model non_emergency 0.50) is shown as 'utility' and R31 (model non_emergency 0.64) as 'medical', while the hover card's /classify bars still show non_emergency on top at 50% and 64% with no explanation - the probability breakdown contradicts the displayed decision. My adversarial inputs make the dispatch consequence explicit: a sensor self-test the model calls non_emergency at 0.86 with package 'none' comes out 'police / police_1' (the keyword default is police), and a 'false alarm, the smoke was burnt toast, no fire, cancel the engine' call comes out 'fire / fire_engine'. The page's How-it-works copy describes only the 0.45 gate and never mentions this veto.
defects.fix: Make the veto conditional and label it. In buildDecision, only fall back to keywords when the model's non_emergency is itself unconfident (categoryConfidence < LOW_CONFIDENCE), and set lowConfidence = true whenever the keyword category replaces the model's, so the hover card's '-> heuristic category' note fires. Close the reverse gap at the same time: when heuristicCategory(text) returns non_emergency (the narrow regex hit), let it win over a confident active label - that alone fixes seed report R29 ('how do I get a copy of a police report I filed last month?', model police 0.80), which currently dispatches police_1. Then add a sentence to the /classify bullet in src/pages/dispatch.astro describing the override.

defects.what: Severity is the weakest of the four judgments: 20/32 exact, 25/32 within one level, stable over two runs. The misses are not symmetric - follow-ups collapse to 0 (R17 0 vs 3, R23 0 vs 3, R27 0 vs 2) while calm reports inflate (R25 3 vs 1, R28 4 vs 2). Severity drives the map pulse, the queue priority, the 'Critical > 60 s' KPI and on-scene time, so a 0 on a live medical follow-up parks it at the back of the queue.
defects.fix: Rewrite the two bottom scale steps so a follow-up about an ongoing emergency cannot read as 'Information only' - for example step 0 "Information only: the caller wants information and nothing is happening" and step 1 "Minor: something happened but nobody is hurt and nothing is at risk now". Re-run smoke.mjs and keep the wording that raises exact agreement; if it will not move, let a merged report inherit the open incident's severity instead of letting a 0 through.

defects.what: Line 70 of the notes says "a 60-second stream of roughly 90 reports costs about 20 batches". generateSchedule(20260917, 60) returns 51 reports, and the map caption in Demo.tsx prints that same 51, so the required How-it-works section contradicts the page it describes. The contract asks the notes to state the batching exactly.
defects.fix: Change to "a 60-second stream of about 50 reports costs roughly 10 batches" (51 reports at ~0.85/s, BATCH_INTERVAL_SECONDS 3 plus a ~2.5 s round trip gives ~10-12 batches), or derive the number from sim.schedule.length so it cannot drift.

defects.what: The brief's dm1_mapping lists eight category labels including duplicate_update. CATEGORY_LABELS ships seven; duplicate_update survives only as a Category type member used by simulatedDecision. The builder replaced it with a separate pair-text /yes-no call and documents why in the notes (putting nearby incidents in the shared text collapsed the category to non_emergency). I judge the substitution an improvement, not a reduction, but it is a deviation from the brief.
defects.fix: No code change needed; keep the current design, the notes already explain it. If exact brief parity is wanted, add duplicate_update back as an eighth label and treat it as a merge signal alongside dupP.

defects.what: Scale is reduced against the brief: RUN_SECONDS 60 with 51 reports, versus the original's 275 reports over 180 simulated seconds. Everything else about the loop is intact.
defects.fix: None. The contract caps auto-running loops at 60 seconds to protect the shared 200 req/min quota, so this reduction is required, not a defect in the port. Worth one line in the notes so a reader comparing with the original README is not surprised.

notes:
Setup: demo/dispatch was already checked out by another worktree, so I verified at a detached HEAD on origin/demo/dispatch (af50300).

Build: `pnpm build` passes with zero errors (3 pages, 1.46 s; only pre-existing zod comment warnings). dist/dispatch/index.html exists and contains the title and the How-it-works section; dist/index.html lists "Dispatch Console".

Smoke: `MS_API_KEY=... node src/demos/dispatch/smoke.mjs` runs clean - 32 reports, 5 calls, 9039 input tokens (282/report), model time 4.0-10.0 s per call, round trip 0.8-2.7 s. Scores: category 29/32 (7 routed to keywords), severity exact 20/32 and within one level 25/32, package 28/32, duplicate 14/18. The builder's reported numbers reproduce.

Four adversarial probes of my own, all through the demo's real request bodies:
(1) Batch alignment - 16 alternating obviously-multi / obviously-single texts. /yes-no and /rate both return results in input order with no drift (0.63/0.60/0.51 on every even row, 0.07/0.41/0.03 on every odd; rate levels 3 0 3 0 ...). The nested {results:[{results:[...]}]} shape the code assumes is correct.
(2) Free-text edge cases - a false-alarm retraction, a heart attack 90 m from an open fire, a mass-casualty bus rollover, a sensor self-test. The rollover and the heart attack are handled well (traffic/ambulance+fire sev 3; medical/ambulance sev 4, with the same-kind guard blocking a 0.67 duplicate). The retraction and the self-test both dispatch units - see the second major defect.
(3) Duplicate hint tuning - all 18 seed pairs under the shipped hints and under a tightened pair: 11/18 vs 16/18. That is the evidence behind the first major defect, so the fix is verified rather than guessed.

Contract, point by point. Met: all five required files plus kpi/sim/triage/MapView helpers, all inside src/demos/dispatch/; meta.ts default export satisfies DemoMeta; demo.css is fully scoped under .d-dispatch (the only top-level rule is an @media block whose children are scoped) and uses the site tokens; the .astro renders <Demo meta><Island client:only="react"><div slot="notes">; no direct fetch, no localStorage, no API key anywhere in the demo files - every call goes through classifyMany/rateMany/dm1; multi-way judgments are /classify with described labels, the ordinal one is /rate on a low-to-high scale, three statements ride in one /yes-no call and up to 16 texts in one call; the .metrics strip shows calls, batches, model time p50 from inferenceMs, round trip p50/p95 from wallMs, tokens and tokens per report; Dm1Error renders inline in .error and the sim keeps running on the keyword fallback; nothing fires on load (running starts false, the feed shows 14 seeded reports and the map draws the city, depots and idle fleet before any call); the run is Start/Stop and stops itself at RUN_SECONDS = 60; live mode pins speed to 1x so 2x/4x cannot raise the request rate; no new dependencies and package.json/pnpm-lock.yaml are untouched (the diff against main is exactly the 10 demo files). Not met: the contract's "tune statements/labels/hints until the answers on the seed data are right" - the duplicate question is not tuned and produces two visible false merges - and the notes' requirement to state the exact batching, which is off by about 40 reports.

Faithfulness to /Users/blaget/projects/milliseconds-demos/briefs/dispatch.json: good. All seven Jev questions are ported (category, severity, multiple victims, hazmat, caller in danger, unit package, duplicate). The interaction loop is intact - three modes with Run all 3, the 40-in-10s surge, 1x/2x/4x speed, the three-column stage, the canvas city with districts, river, depots, pulsing incidents and moving units, the event log, the per-report probability hover card, and the six-row comparison table with exactly the brief's metrics. The data is the original generator, city, rng and types merged verbatim into data.ts on seed 20260917, and heuristicDecision, heuristicPackage, simulatedDecision and nearestOpen are the experiment's code unchanged. Two deviations, both defensible and both listed above: the 60 s / 51 report run (contract-mandated) and duplicate_update moving out of the label set into a dedicated pair call.

Verdict: pass=false on two major defects. Neither blocks the build or the smoke run; both are answer-quality problems on the demo's central claim, and both have concrete fixes - the duplicate one already measured at 16/18.

I made no changes to the branch and pushed nothing. I wrote four throwaway probe scripts in the worktree and deleted all of them; the only thing git reports is a pre-existing modified .DS_Store I did not touch.
